newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican bullfighter dies with head crushed.
newsitem.headline: Mexican bullfighter dies with head crushed.

text.p: Mexican mounted bullfighter Eduardo Funtanet died on Tuesday of massive head injuries sustained when his horse tumbled on top of him as he fought a bull, a hospital spokesman said.

Funtanet, 33, had been in a coma since the accident during a bullfight on Sunday. He died of brain injuries, a fractured skull and damage to the carotid artery in the neck, a spokesman for Mexico City's ABC Hospital said.

Spectators in the city's huge Plaza Mexico bullring -- the world's largest -- watched horrified on Sunday as the 1073-pound (488 kg) bull charged Funtanet's horse, knocking its hind legs out from under it and sending the bullfighter flying.
The horse rolled over on top of Funtanet and its heavy leather saddle crushed his skull.
A spokeswoman for the bullring said it was the first human fatality in the Plaza Mexico "in many years".

Funtanet began his professional career in 1985 as a "rejoneador", a special kind of mounted bullfighter who taunts and injures the bull by jabbing it with an iron lance from an unprotected horse before killing it.
The art of "rejoneo" began in Portugal and is much less common than the regular Spanish-style bullfight, where the matador does all the work standing in the ring.
Funtanet is survived by his wife and three children, including a baby born just two months ago.
